QUERIES: "Camp Kanawana" ; "ce camp existe toujours" ; "c'est maintenant le camp Kanawana" ;
         "En 1911, le Camp Nominingue" ; "Connu longtemps sous le nom d'Otoreke" ;
         "camp, sur l'une des trois iles" ; "s'installe sur la rive de ce grand" ;
         "trois iles" "Otoreke"

RECONSTRUCTED (accents as the OCR gives them):

  ... travaillent a l'installation de ce premier camp, sur l'une des trois iles. Connu longtemps
  sous le nom d'Otoreke, ce camp existe toujours: c'est maintenant le camp Kanawana. En 1911, le
  Camp Nominingue, le premier camp franco[-]phone, s'installe sur la rive de ce grand lac des
  Laurentides. L'année suivante ...

TWO FURTHER SENTENCES FROM THE SAME BOOK, returned by the query "trois iles" "Otoreke" and not
joined to the passage above:

  "... la Colonie des Grèves a Contrecoeur et le camp Otoreke a Saint-Adolphe-d'Howard, au nord
   de Montréal."
  "... leur premier voyage en train pour aller au camp Otoreke a Saint-Adolphe-d'Howard dans les
   Laurentides ..."
  "... l'extérieur de la ville. C'est le cas du camp Otoreke dans les Laurentides et de la
   colonie de vacances ..."

WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT, stated here so the correction travels with the quotation:
  Kanawana is at Saint-Sauveur and Mille-Isles, about thirty kilometres from Saint-Adolphe-
  d'Howard. The sentence says the ISLAND SITE is now Kanawana, and it is not. It also erases
  Camp Otoreke's own history: the main boys' camp moved to the Kanawana site in 1910 and Otoreke
  went on operating at Lac Saint-Joseph for more than seventy years afterwards, as an adult and
  family camp, until 1982. What the sentence gets right is that the INSTITUTION that began on
  the islands continues as Kanawana.

  Separately: the book dates Camp Nominingue to 1911 as "le premier camp francophone". The
  Quebec Camping Association's own 1974-75 directory gives Nominingue's founding as 1925. The
  two may be measuring different things. Neither is preferred here.
